money.body: Sells you an outcome and skips the skill. When the trend moves on, you're left with a course and no habit.

custom.title: Your own curriculum

story.headline: Why we started this
story.body: In 2019 a friend at OpenAI got me into an early API program, a year before ChatGPT existed. I've built with AI every day since. Friends started asking me to set up their systems. They got 10+ hours a week back, and they all said the same thing: you should teach this. So we did.

platform.headline: AI changes daily. Keeping up is a job.
platform.body: New models, new tools, a dozen papers before lunch. It's hard to follow even for us, and following it is our work. So we built the place where you don't have to do it alone.

structure.headline: How the twelve weeks run
structure.body: Three blocks of four weeks: Foundations, Build, Deepen and capstone. Each block can be booked on its own.

blocks.title: Weeks 1 to 3, the spine
blocks.line: How these systems work: pipelines, agents, memory, harnesses, the compound loop. Your tools set up. A map of your own week, and the three tasks worth automating first.

blocks.title: Weeks 4 to 10, your track
blocks.line: Seven weeks on the work your track is made of. Weeks 4 and 5 go deep on the track's highest-value workflow. Week 9 is verification: catching what the assistant got wrong. Week 10 draws your personal system map and plans the capstone.

blocks.title: Weeks 11 to 12, capstone
blocks.line: One fully running system on your real job. The same task before and after, with the artifacts to prove it. Then a handoff into the platform.

week.headline: How a session runs
week.body: Two hours, once a week, the same shape every time, so nobody has to learn the class, only the content.

rules: At least half of every session is you building on your own material, from a template, never from a blank page.

The assignment is real work, logged: a task from your job done the new way, with time and output recorded. Those logs are your before and after.

paths.headline: Two technical paths

items.title: Browser-only
items.line: Every track. Your assistant in the browser, your company's own suite, nothing installed. The path for corporate IT that blocks everything else.

items.line: From week 3, for people who can run their own setup: a rented server, an always-on agent, open-source tools. Lives fully in the startup track.

paths.note: We teach with the same tools we run our own companies on, at the tiers a learner actually needs. The picks are dated and swapped when they stop being the best pick. The method doesn't change.

measure.headline: Measured, not felt
measure.body: You log a baseline in week one. In week twelve you show the same task before and after: both outputs, both durations, one quality checklist. Nobody graduates on "I feel faster."

items.q: Do I need to know how to code?

paragraphs: I've been interested in AI since my early years in tech. In 2019 a friend who was a researcher and developer at OpenAI, working on GPT-2 back then, told me about the researcher program for testing the first GPT-3 APIs. That was a year before ChatGPT was public. I got in.

Since then my team of developers and I have used AI every day, and it has changed how I interact with technology. We use it for things I could not have done alone a couple of years ago, some of them ridiculous.

My normal friends, founders, solopreneurs, lawyers, writers, people in finance and design, creators, asked me to help set up their systems. When I did, they saved tens of hours a week and their output exploded in speed and quality. After a few weeks most of them said the same thing: why don't you sell this, or teach it.

To me that was a crazy idea. All I do in my free time is read about new developments to improve my own systems. I've read more research papers on AI in the last three years than papers of any kind in the previous thirty. And that is how we decided to build InnovLabs, with one of the very people I taught and built their first AI workflows with.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: InnovLabs ("we") keeps this policy under Korea's Personal Information Protection Act to protect your personal data and handle any concern quickly. It covers processing on innovlab.me and app.innovlab.me. The Korean version is the binding one; this translation is for convenience.
privacy.contact_form: Ask through the companies inquiry form

sections.heading: 1. What we collect and why
paragraphs: We collect personal data only in the situations below, and use it for nothing beyond the stated purpose.
items: Companies inquiry form (innovlab.me): name, company, title (optional), email, area of interest, team size (optional), message (optional), browser information. Purpose: to reply and to run training or development consultations.

Survey and profile (app.innovlab.me): survey answers, entry path (office worker, solopreneur, student), and an organization code if you arrived through a company invite. Purpose: to recommend a track and generate your report.
Registration (app.innovlab.me): email, Kakao or Google login identifier, consent time and version, newsletter opt-in. Purpose: account management, course and report notices.
Waitlists (student and solopreneur courses): email, short answers, newsletter opt-in. Purpose: to tell you when the course opens.
Collected automatically: server access logs (IP address, time). Purpose: security and error handling. We run no analytics or advertising cookies today; this policy is updated before any are added.

sections.heading: 2. How long we keep it
paragraphs: Data is deleted without delay once its purpose is met. By item:
items: Company inquiries: up to one year after the reply is complete, or immediately on request.
Account, survey answers, reports: until you close the account or ask for deletion.
Waitlists: until the course notice goes out or you ask for deletion.
Server logs: three months.
Where another law requires longer retention, only for that period and only that data.

sections.heading: 3. Sharing with third parties
paragraphs: We do not provide or sell personal data to third parties. The only exception is a lawful request from an authority under Korean law.

sections.heading: 4. Processors and overseas transfer
paragraphs: We rely on the providers below to run the service, and your data is stored or processed on their servers outside Korea. Transfer happens over the network when you use the service; retention equals the engagement period.
items: Supabase, Inc.: database and login hosting. Items: everything in section 1. Location: the provider's data centers (United States and others).
DigitalOcean, LLC: web server hosting. Items: access logs, company inquiries. Location: the provider's data centers.
Anthropic, PBC: processing survey answers to generate your report. Items: survey answers only, never your name or email. Location: United States.
Kakao, Google: social login. Items: account identifier. Their own privacy policies apply.

sections.heading: 5. Your rights
paragraphs: You may at any time request access, correction, deletion, or suspension of processing, and withdraw consent you have given. Contact us below; we act within ten days and tell you the result. Data of children under 14 is collected only with a legal guardian's consent, and the guardian may exercise the same rights.

sections.heading: 6. Deletion
paragraphs: Electronic files are deleted in a way that cannot be recovered. We keep no paper records.

sections.heading: 7. Security measures
items: Access rights are kept to a minimum, with row-level access control on the database.
All traffic is encrypted over HTTPS.
Company clients see only aggregates of five or more people, never an individual's answers.

sections.heading: 8. Privacy officer
paragraphs: Eric, co-founder of InnovLabs. For questions, access or deletion requests, and complaints, reach us below.

sections.heading: 9. Where else to turn
paragraphs: If you need independent advice or want to report our handling, these Korean bodies take cases.
items: Personal Information Infringement Report Center: privacy.kisa.or.kr, 118
Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee: kopico.go.kr, 1833-6972
Supreme Prosecutors' Office cybercrime unit: spo.go.kr, 1301
National Police Agency cyber bureau: ecrm.police.go.kr, 182

sections.heading: 10. Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We announce changes on this page seven days before they take effect and show the effective date. A material change to what we collect or why means asking for consent again.
